key_findings.finding: Most plausible reagent classes for preserving the adjacent alkene are mild, chemoselective carbonyl hydride reductions—especially NaBH4 in MeOH or EtOH, preferably Luche conditions (NaBH4/CeCl3) for an enone; alternatives include DIBAL-H under controlled low-temperature conditions, or a catalytic asymmetric borane/CBS reduction when stereocontrol is needed. Avoid H2/Pd, Pt, or Ni if alkene preservation is required because those conditions can hydrogenate C=C; LiAlH4 is less chemoselective and may be unnecessarily harsh for heteroaromatic substrates.
